c1s1.title: Basic Greetings
c1s1.intro: Greetings are the first thing you say when you meet someone. In English, the greeting you use depends on the time of day and how well you know the person.

sections.heading: Essential Greetings
sections.body: These are the most common English greetings. Use them when you first see or meet someone.
sections.tip: "Good night" is only used when saying goodbye late at night, not as a greeting.

sections.heading: Time-based Greetings
sections.body: English greetings change depending on the time of day. Memorise this simple pattern:
sections.tip: When in doubt, "Hello" or "Hi" works at ANY time of day.

sections.heading: How to Pronounce
sections.body: Listen carefully to the stress in each greeting. The stressed syllable is shown in CAPS.
sections.tip: Smile when you say hello — it makes your English sound more natural and friendly!

content.question: Apa artinya 'Good afternoon'?
content.explanation: "Good afternoon" = Selamat siang, used between noon and 5 PM.

content.hint: Say: Good morning!

c1s2.title: Polite Expressions
c1s2.intro: Polite expressions are the foundation of good English manners. Using words like 'please', 'thank you', and 'sorry' will make you sound natural and respectful in any situation.

sections.heading: Key Polite Words
sections.body: These four expressions are used every day in English. Learn them well!
sections.tip: Always say 'please' at the end of a request: "Can you help me, please?"

sections.heading: How to Use Them
sections.body: Here are common sentence patterns using polite expressions:

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?

sections.tip: "Excuse me" is for getting someone's attention or getting past them. "Sorry" is for apologising.

sections.heading: Quick Dialogue
sections.body: See how polite expressions flow naturally in conversation:

examples.en: A: Excuse me, can you help me please?
B: Of course! What do you need?
examples.id: B: Tentu! Apa yang kamu butuhkan?

content.explanation: "Excuse me" is used to politely get someone's attention or to ask for help.

content.hint: Say: Thank you very much!

c1s3.title: Introducing Yourself
c1s3.intro: The first thing you tell a new person is your name. English has simple, friendly phrases for introducing yourself. Mastering these will help you start any conversation confidently.

sections.heading: Introduction Phrases
sections.body: Use these phrases when you meet someone for the first time:
sections.tip: "Nice to meet you" is the polite response when someone introduces themselves to you.

sections.heading: Name Introduction Pattern
sections.body: There are two common ways to introduce your name in English:

examples.en: Hi! I'm Dian. Nice to meet you!
examples.id: Hai! Saya Dian. Senang bertemu denganmu!

sections.tip: "I'm" is the contracted form of "I am" — used in casual speech.

sections.heading: First Meeting Dialogue
sections.body: A natural introduction sounds like this:

examples.en: A: Hi! My name is Sari.
B: Hello Sari! I am Budi.
A: Nice to meet you, Budi!
B: Nice to meet you too!

content.sentence: ___ name is Sari. I am from Bali.
content.explanation: "My" menunjukkan kepemilikan — "My name is" = nama saya adalah.

content.hint: Say: Nice to meet you!

c1s4.title: Basic Pronouns
c1s4.intro: Pronouns replace nouns so we don't have to repeat names. English has clear, simple pronouns for every person. Knowing them is essential for building any sentence.

sections.heading: Subject Pronouns
sections.body: Subject pronouns tell us WHO does the action in a sentence.
sections.tip: "It" is for animals and things. "He" and "She" are only for people.

sections.heading: Pronouns in Sentences
sections.body: Replace the noun with the correct pronoun:

examples.en: Budi is a student → He is a student.
examples.id: Budi adalah pelajar → Dia adalah pelajar.

examples.en: Sari is my friend → She is my friend.
examples.id: Sari adalah temanku → Dia adalah temanku.

examples.en: Budi and I study → We study.
examples.id: Budi dan saya belajar → Kami belajar.

sections.tip: Use "They" for a group of people, regardless of gender.

content.sentence: ___ is my teacher. His name is Mr. Budi.
content.explanation: "His name" shows the teacher is male, so we use "He".

content.hint: Say: I am a student.

c1s5.title: Simple Sentences with Am / Is
c1s5.intro: The verb 'to be' (am, is, are) is the most important verb in English. It connects a subject to a description. Let's master 'am' and 'is' first.

sections.heading: When to Use Am vs Is
sections.body: The verb 'to be' changes depending on the subject. Study this pattern carefully:
sections.tip: ONLY use 'am' with 'I'. Use 'is' with he, she, and it.

sections.heading: Simple Descriptions
sections.body: Use am / is + adjective to describe yourself or someone else:
sections.tip: The structure is: Subject + am/is + [adjective or noun].

content.explanation: "Am" is only used with "I". Never say "I is" or "I are".

content.hint: Say: I am happy.

c1s6.title: Chapter 1 Review — Putting It Together
c1s6.intro: You've learned greetings, polite words, introductions, pronouns, and am/is. Now let's see how they work together in real conversation.

sections.heading: Full Introduction Dialogue
sections.body: Read this conversation and notice how everything from Chapter 1 comes together:

examples.en: A: Good morning! My name is Rina.
examples.id: A: Selamat pagi! Nama saya Rina.

examples.en: B: Hello Rina! I am Budi. Nice to meet you!
examples.id: B: Halo Rina! Saya Budi. Senang bertemu denganmu!

examples.en: A: Nice to meet you too, Budi!
examples.id: A: Senang bertemu denganmu juga, Budi!

examples.en: B: I am a student. Are you a student too?
examples.id: B: Saya adalah pelajar. Apakah kamu juga pelajar?

examples.en: A: Yes, I am! Goodbye, Budi!
examples.id: A: Ya, saya! Sampai jumpa, Budi!

sections.heading: Chapter 1 Quick Review
sections.body: Key patterns from this chapter:

examples.en: Polite: Please / Thank you / Sorry / Excuse me
examples.id: Sopan: Tolong / Terima kasih / Maaf / Permisi

examples.en: Introduce: My name is … / Nice to meet you
Pronouns: I / You / He / She / We / They
examples.id: Kata ganti: Saya / Kamu / Dia / Kami / Mereka

examples.en: To be: I am … / He is … / She is …
examples.id: Kata kerja: Saya adalah … / Dia adalah …

sections.tip: Practice saying a full introduction out loud every day — it will become natural very quickly!

content.question: Lengkapi: 'Thank you!' — '___!'
content.explanation: The correct response to 'Thank you' is 'You're welcome' (Sama-sama).

content.phrase: My name is Rina. Nice to meet you!
content.hint: Say: My name is [your name]. Nice to meet you!
content.translation: Nama saya Rina. Senang bertemu denganmu!

c2s1.title: Objects Around Us
c2s1.intro: Knowing the names of everyday objects is one of the fastest ways to grow your vocabulary. In this stage, we focus on things you see at school and home every day.

sections.heading: Classroom & Home Objects
sections.body: These are common objects you'll find at school and at home:

examples.id: I use a book to study.
The book is on the table.
I use a pen to write.
I carry my books in my bag.
She puts her phone in her bag.

sections.tip: When learning object names, point to the real object and say the English word out loud.

sections.heading: Using 'The' and 'A'
sections.body: English uses articles before nouns. 'A' = one unspecified thing. 'The' = a specific thing.

examples.en: The book is on the table. (specific book)
examples.id: Buku itu ada di atas meja.

examples.en: She has a bag. → The bag is blue.
examples.id: Dia punya tas. → Tas itu biru.

sections.tip: Use 'a' the first time you mention something. Use 'the' after that, when it's clear which one you mean.

content.explanation: A pen is used for writing. A book is for reading, a chair is for sitting.

content.phrase: The book is on the table.
content.hint: Say: The book is on the table.
content.translation: Buku itu ada di atas meja.

c2s2.title: Food & Drink
c2s2.intro: Food and drink vocabulary is incredibly useful for daily conversation — whether you're at a restaurant, a canteen, or just talking about your day.

sections.heading: Common Food & Drink Words
sections.body: Memorise these essential food and drink words:

examples.id: Can I have a glass of water?
I like coffee in the morning.
She eats an apple after school.
I eat an egg for breakfast.

sections.tip: Practice ordering food by saying: "Can I have [food], please?"

sections.heading: Talking About Meals
sections.body: Use these patterns to talk about what you eat and drink:

examples.id: Saya makan nasi untuk makan siang.

examples.en: Can I have a glass of water?

sections.tip: "Eat" is for solid food. "Drink" is for liquids. Don't mix them up!

content.sentence: I drink ___ every morning for breakfast.
content.explanation: "Drink" is used with liquids. Milk (susu) is a common breakfast drink.

content.hint: Say: I eat rice every day.

c2s3.title: Colors
c2s3.intro: Colors are some of the most useful adjectives in English. They let you describe objects, clothing, and your surroundings. Colors come BEFORE the noun they describe.

sections.heading: Basic Colors
sections.body: Learn all the basic English colors and their Indonesian equivalents:
sections.tip: The Indonesian flag is red (merah) and white (putih) — Merah Putih!

sections.heading: Color + Noun Pattern
sections.body: In English, the color always comes BEFORE the noun (opposite to Indonesian):

examples.id: pensil kuning saya → my yellow pencil

sections.tip: Remember: English word order for adjectives is reversed compared to Indonesian!

content.question: Apa bahasa Inggrisnya 'Hitam'?
content.explanation: Black = Hitam. White = Putih. Blue = Biru. Green = Hijau.

content.hint: Say: I have a red bag.

c2s4.title: Numbers 1–10
c2s4.intro: Numbers are essential for everyday communication — telling the time, shopping, and giving your age. Let's master the numbers from one to ten.

sections.heading: Numbers 1–10
sections.body: Memorise these numbers and how to pronounce them:

examples.id: There are seven days in a week.

sections.tip: To say your age: I am [number] years old. — "I am fifteen years old."

sections.heading: Numbers in Sentences
sections.body: Use numbers directly before the noun they count:
sections.tip: After a number, the noun is usually plural (add -s): one cat → two cats.

content.question: Apa bahasa Inggrisnya angka 4?
content.explanation: Four = 4 (Empat). Three = 3, Five = 5, Six = 6.

content.hint: Say: I have three cats.

c2s5.title: This is / That is
c2s5.intro: "This" and "That" are demonstrative pronouns — they point to things. "This" points to something NEAR you, "That" points to something FAR away.

sections.heading: This vs That
sections.body: The difference is simple — it's all about distance:

examples.en: That is a big mountain. (far away)

sections.tip: Simple rule: THIS = near (ini), THAT = far (itu).

sections.heading: Describing with This/That
sections.body: Combine 'this/that' with a color and noun for fuller descriptions:

examples.en: That is a big white house.

sections.tip: Pattern: This/That + is + a/an + [color] + [noun]

content.sentence: ___ is a big mountain far away.
content.explanation: "That" points to something far away. "This" is for things nearby.

content.hint: Say: This is a red apple.

c2s6.title: Chapter 2 Review — Objects, Colors & Numbers
c2s6.intro: Time to review everything from Chapter 2! You've learned objects, food, colors, numbers, and how to use 'this/that'. Let's combine them into rich descriptions.

sections.heading: Building Rich Descriptions
sections.body: Combine numbers, colors, and objects to make detailed sentences:
sections.tip: Pattern: number + color + noun (e.g. three blue pens)

sections.heading: Chapter 2 Word List
sections.body: Key vocabulary from this chapter:

examples.en: Objects: book, chair, table, pen, bag, phone
examples.id: Buku, kursi, meja, pena, tas, HP

examples.en: Food: rice, bread, water, milk, coffee, apple
examples.id: Nasi, roti, air, susu, kopi, apel

examples.en: Colors: red, blue, green, yellow, white, black
examples.id: Merah, biru, hijau, kuning, putih, hitam

examples.en: Numbers: one, two, three, four, five … ten
examples.id: Satu, dua, tiga, empat, lima … sepuluh

content.question: Terjemahkan: 'Ini adalah apel merah.'
content.explanation: "Ini" = This (nearby), "apel merah" = red apple. Correct: This is a red apple.

content.hint: Say: This is a green bag.

c3s1.title: Common Action Verbs
c3s1.intro: Verbs are the heart of every sentence — they express actions. Knowing the most common English action verbs lets you describe almost anything you do in a day.

sections.heading: Top Action Verbs
sections.body: These are the most frequently used action verbs in everyday English:

examples.id: I go to school every day.
He watches a movie on Saturday.

sections.tip: For he/she/it, add -s to the verb: I eat → He eats. I go → She goes.

sections.heading: Subject + Verb Sentences
sections.body: Use subject + verb to build simple action sentences:

examples.en: I go to school every day.
examples.id: Saya pergi ke sekolah setiap hari.

examples.en: She sees a movie every Saturday.

examples.id: Kami belajar bahasa Inggris di sekolah.

sections.tip: "Every day" means habitual action. Put it at the end of the sentence.

content.sentence: I ___ to school by bus every morning.
content.explanation: "Go to school" is the correct phrase. "Eat to school" doesn't make sense.

content.phrase: I go to school every day.
content.hint: Say: I go to school every day.
content.translation: Saya pergi ke sekolah setiap hari.

c3s2.title: Daily Activities & Routines
c3s2.intro: Talking about your daily routine is one of the most common topics in English conversation. Let's learn how to describe what you do from morning to night.

sections.heading: Morning Routine Verbs
sections.body: These verbs describe what most people do in the morning:

examples.en: Go to school — Pergi ke sekolah

sections.tip: Use "at" before clock times: wake up AT six, sleep AT ten.

sections.heading: Routine Sentence Pattern
sections.body: To describe a routine, use: subject + verb + time/frequency:

examples.en: I wake up at five every morning.
examples.id: Saya bangun jam lima setiap pagi.

examples.en: He goes to school at half past eight.
examples.id: Dia pergi ke sekolah jam delapan setengah.

sections.tip: "After school" and "before school" are very useful phrases for describing your day.

content.sentence: I ___ at 10 PM and wake up at 5 AM.
content.explanation: "Sleep at 10 PM" means you go to bed at 10. "Wake up at 5 AM" is the opposite.

content.hint: Say: I wake up at six.

c3s3.title: Time Expressions
c3s3.intro: To talk about WHEN things happen, you need time expressions. These small words and phrases — morning, afternoon, today, tomorrow — anchor your sentences in time.

sections.heading: Time of Day
sections.body: These words describe different parts of the day:

examples.id: Good morning! I exercise every morning.
I eat lunch in the afternoon.
Good evening! We study in the evening.

sections.tip: Use "in the" before morning/afternoon/evening: IN the morning, IN the afternoon.

sections.heading: Day Words
sections.body: These words tell you WHEN something happens relative to today:
sections.tip: "See you tomorrow!" = Sampai jumpa besok! — a very common farewell.

content.sentence: I have a test ___. I need to study tonight.
content.explanation: "Tomorrow" = besok. If you need to study tonight, the test is tomorrow.

content.hint: Say: See you tomorrow!

c3s4.title: Talking About Your Routine
c3s4.intro: Now we combine verbs, time expressions, and clock times to describe a full daily routine. This is one of the most common conversation topics in English.

sections.heading: Clock Time Patterns
sections.body: Here's how to say what you do at specific times:
sections.tip: Use AT + clock time. Use IN THE + morning / afternoon / evening.

sections.heading: Sharing Your Routine
sections.body: Here's how a routine conversation sounds:

examples.en: A: When do you wake up?
B: I wake up at six every morning.
examples.id: B: Saya bangun jam enam setiap pagi.

examples.en: A: What do you do after school?
examples.id: A: Apa yang kamu lakukan setelah sekolah?

examples.en: B: I go home and study.
A: What time do you sleep?
B: I sleep at ten at night.
examples.id: B: Saya tidur jam sepuluh malam.

content.question: Terjemahkan: 'Saya makan malam pukul 7.'
content.explanation: Makan malam = dinner. Pukul 7 = at seven. So: I eat dinner at seven.

content.hint: Say: I eat breakfast at eight.

c3s5.title: Asking Simple Questions
c3s5.intro: Question words (who, what, where, when) are the key to asking about anything. With just these four words, you can start almost any conversation in English.

sections.heading: The 4 Core Question Words
sections.body: Memorise these four and you can ask about almost anything:

examples.id: What is this? / What do you eat?
Where do you live? / Where is the school?
When do you sleep? / When is the test?
Who is your teacher? / Who is that?

sections.tip: Question word + do/does + subject + verb: What do you eat for breakfast?

sections.heading: Question Structure
sections.body: Basic pattern: Question word + do/does + subject + verb

examples.en: What do you eat for breakfast?
examples.id: Apa yang kamu makan untuk sarapan?

examples.en: Where do you go after school?
examples.id: Ke mana kamu pergi setelah sekolah?

sections.tip: "Do" is used with I/you/we/they. "Does" is used with he/she/it.

content.sentence: ___ is your favorite subject at school?
content.explanation: "What" asks about things. "What is your favorite subject?" = Apa mata pelajaran favoritmu?

content.phrase: What do you eat for breakfast?
content.hint: Say: What do you eat for breakfast?
content.translation: Apa yang kamu makan untuk sarapan?

c3s6.title: Chapter 3 Review — Daily Activities
c3s6.intro: You've covered verbs, daily routines, time expressions, and question words. Now combine them to describe your full day and ask questions about others' routines.

sections.heading: Full Routine Conversation
sections.body: Read this dialogue using everything from Chapter 3:

examples.en: A: When do you wake up every day?
examples.id: A: Jam berapa kamu bangun setiap hari?

examples.en: B: I wake up at six. Then I eat breakfast.
examples.id: B: Saya bangun jam enam. Lalu saya sarapan.

examples.en: A: What do you do after school?
examples.id: A: Apa yang kamu lakukan setelah sekolah?

examples.en: B: I go home and study every night.
examples.id: B: Saya pulang dan belajar setiap malam.

examples.en: A: What time do you sleep?
B: I sleep at ten. See you tomorrow!
examples.id: B: Saya tidur jam sepuluh. Sampai jumpa besok!

sections.heading: Chapter 3 Patterns Summary
sections.body: Key grammar from this chapter:
sections.tip: To sound fluent, chain activities: "I wake up, eat breakfast, then go to school."

content.sentence: ___ do you wake up every day?
content.explanation: "When" asks about time. "When do you wake up?" = Kapan/jam berapa kamu bangun?

content.hint: Say: I study every night.

c4s1.title: Basic Adjectives
c4s1.intro: Adjectives describe people, places, and things. They make your English more expressive and detailed. The most useful adjectives come in opposite pairs.

sections.heading: Core Adjective Pairs
sections.body: Learn adjectives in pairs — it doubles your vocabulary instantly:

examples.id: This is a big dog. That is a small cat.
She is a good student. The weather is bad.
I am very happy today. She looks sad.
The coffee is hot. The water is cold.
He runs fast. The bus is slow.

sections.tip: Add "very" before an adjective to make it stronger: very big, very happy.

sections.heading: Adjective Position
sections.body: In English, adjectives go BEFORE the noun OR after 'to be':

examples.en: Before noun: a big dog, a happy student
examples.id: seekor anjing besar, seorang pelajar yang bahagia

examples.en: After 'to be': The dog is big. She is happy.
With 'very': I am very happy today.

sections.tip: Both positions are correct. "A big house" and "The house is big" are both fine.

content.sentence: This is a ___ dog. It is not small at all.
content.explanation: "Not small" means the dog is big. Big is the antonym of small.

content.hint: Say: I am very happy today.

c4s2.title: Physical Descriptions
c4s2.intro: Describing physical appearance is a key conversation skill. In English, you can describe height, age, and build using simple adjectives with 'to be'.

sections.heading: Physical Adjectives
sections.body: These adjectives describe how people look:

examples.id: My brother is very tall. My sister is short.
She is young. My grandmother is old.
The baby is small and cute.
He is handsome. She is pretty.

sections.tip: "Handsome" is usually for men. "Pretty" or "beautiful" is usually for women.

sections.heading: Describing with Multiple Adjectives
sections.body: Use 'and' to connect two or more adjectives:

examples.en: He is tall, strong, and handsome.
My grandmother is old but very wise.
examples.id: Nenekku sudah tua tapi sangat bijaksana.

sections.tip: Use commas when listing three or more adjectives: tall, strong, and handsome.

content.sentence: He is very ___ — almost two meters!
content.explanation: Two meters is very tall! "Almost two meters" = sangat tinggi.

content.hint: Say: She is tall and young.

c4s3.title: Describing Objects
c4s3.intro: You can combine size, color, and adjectives to build detailed descriptions of any object. This is the foundation of descriptive English.

sections.heading: Adjective Order Rule
sections.body: When using multiple adjectives, English has a specific order: size → color → noun

examples.en: a small white cat (size + color + noun)

sections.tip: General rule: Opinion → Size → Color → Noun. (e.g. a beautiful small white cat)

sections.heading: More Useful Adjectives
sections.body: Expand your description vocabulary with these words:

content.question: Terjemahkan: 'Ini adalah tas hitam.'
content.explanation: Ini = This (nearby). Tas hitam = black bag. So: This is a black bag.

content.phrase: I have a small white cat.
content.hint: Say: I have a small white cat.

c4s4.title: Using Is / Are
c4s4.intro: You've mastered 'am' and 'is'. Now we add 'are' — used for plural subjects and for 'you'. Together, am/is/are form the complete 'to be' verb.

sections.heading: Complete To Be Chart
sections.body: Memorise this complete pattern:
sections.tip: Quick rule: IS for one person/thing (he, she, it). ARE for more than one OR 'you'.

sections.heading: Is vs Are in Sentences
sections.body: See the difference in context:

examples.en: This book is thick. (one thing → is)
My friend is kind. (one person → is)

sections.tip: When the subject ends in -s (friends, students, parents), use ARE.

content.sentence: My parents ___ very kind and loving.
content.explanation: "My parents" = two people = plural → use "are". (My mother IS, but my parents ARE.)

content.hint: Say: They are my best friends.

c4s5.title: Simple Descriptions
c4s5.intro: Now we bring it all together — subjects, to be, and adjectives — to write clear, complete sentences that describe people, animals, and things.

sections.heading: Description Sentence Pattern
sections.body: The core pattern: Subject + is/are + adjective(s)

examples.en: The sky is blue and clear.
The water is cold and clean.
The students are smart and hardworking.
examples.id: Para pelajar itu pintar dan rajin.

sections.tip: You can stack adjectives: The apple is red AND sweet AND delicious.

sections.heading: Describing Things Around You
sections.body: Practice describing things you see every day:

examples.en: A: What is the weather like today?
B: It is hot and sunny.
A: What is your classroom like?
B: It is big, clean, and very bright.
examples.id: B: Besar, bersih, dan sangat terang.

content.question: Terjemahkan: 'Hari ini cuacanya panas dan cerah.'
options: Today the weather is cold and rainy.
Today the weather is hot and sunny.
The weather is good and big.
content.correctAnswer: Today the weather is hot and sunny.
content.explanation: Panas = hot, cerah = sunny. "Today the weather is hot and sunny." is correct.

content.hint: Say: The apple is red.

c4s6.title: Chapter 4 Review — Describing People & Things
c4s6.intro: You've mastered adjectives, physical descriptions, adjective order, and the full 'to be' verb. Now write rich, complete descriptions of anything!

sections.heading: Full Description Formula
sections.body: Combine everything for a powerful description:

examples.en: The garden is beautiful and green.
My friend is short and funny.
She is young, tall, and cheerful.
The students are smart and hardworking.
examples.id: Para pelajar itu pintar dan rajin.

sections.tip: Great description = subject + is/are + [size] + [appearance] + [personality]

sections.heading: Describing a Friend
sections.body: Practice describing someone you know:

examples.en: A: Tell me about your best friend!
B: My friend is tall and funny.
A: What does she look like?
B: She is young, and she has a big, beautiful smile.
examples.id: B: Dia muda dan punya senyum besar yang indah.

content.question: Terjemahkan: 'Temanku pendek dan lucu.'
options: My friend is tall and funny.
My friend is short and funny.
My friend is short and sad.
My friend is young and small.
content.correctAnswer: My friend is short and funny.
content.explanation: Pendek = short, lucu = funny. "My friend is short and funny."

content.phrase: My friend is short and funny.
content.hint: Say: My friend is short and funny.

c5s1.title: Personal Questions
c5s1.intro: When you meet someone new, the conversation almost always includes personal questions about name, origin, and age. Let's master how to ask AND answer these questions confidently.

sections.heading: Key Personal Questions
sections.body: These are the most common questions people ask when getting to know someone:
sections.tip: The most common response to "How are you?" is "I'm fine, thank you!" or "I'm good, thanks!"

sections.heading: Answering Personal Questions
sections.body: Pattern for answering personal questions:

examples.en: Q: What is your name? → A: My name is Budi.
Q: Where are you from? → A: I am from Bali.
Q: How old are you? → A: I am fifteen years old.
Q: How are you? → A: I am fine, thank you!
examples.id: Apa kabar? → Saya baik, terima kasih!

sections.tip: Always answer in full sentences — it sounds more natural and shows confidence.

content.sentence: How ___ you? — I am fine, thank you!
content.explanation: "How are you?" is the standard greeting question. Answer: I am fine, thank you!

content.hint: Say: Where are you from?

c5s2.title: Answering About Yourself
c5s2.intro: The ability to introduce yourself fully — name, origin, and age — is the foundation of all social English. Let's build a complete self-introduction.

sections.heading: Full Self-Introduction
sections.body: Here's a complete introduction you can use immediately:

examples.en: I am a student at SMP 5.

sections.tip: For age: I am [number] years old. — "I am fifteen years old."

sections.heading: Yes/No Questions with Is/Are
sections.body: Yes/No questions flip the subject and to be verb:

examples.en: Are you a student? → Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
Is she your sister? → Yes, she is. / No, she isn't.
Are they your friends? → Yes, they are.

sections.tip: Short answers: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not. Don't just say "Yes" or "No" — add the pronoun and verb.

content.sentence: My name ___ Sari and I ___ from Yogyakarta.
content.explanation: My name IS (3rd person singular) + I AM (1st person). Pattern: is / am.

content.phrase: My name is Reza. I am from Jakarta.
content.hint: Say: My name is [name]. I am from [city].
content.translation: Nama saya Reza. Saya dari Jakarta.

c5s3.title: Asking About Things
c5s3.intro: "What is this?" and "What is that?" are two of the most useful questions in English. You can use them to learn the name of anything you see.

sections.heading: Questions About Objects
sections.body: Use these questions to ask about things around you:

examples.id: Use for something FAR from you.

examples.en: Whose is this? — Ini milik siapa?
Is this yours? — Apakah ini milikmu?

sections.tip: If you don't know the English name for something, just point and say "What is this?"

sections.heading: Asking & Answering
sections.body: Natural conversations about objects:

examples.en: A: What is this? — It is a dictionary.
A: What is that? — That is a new smartphone.
examples.id: A: Apa itu? — Itu HP baru.

examples.en: A: Is this your bag? — Yes, it is!
A: Whose pen is this? — It is mine.

content.sentence: — ___ is this? — It is a dictionary.
content.explanation: "What" asks about things. "What is this?" = Apa ini? The answer is the name of the object.

content.hint: Say: What is this?

c5s4.title: Asking About Preferences
c5s4.intro: "Do you like…?" is one of the most common ways to start a conversation and find common interests. Master this pattern and you'll never run out of things to talk about.

sections.heading: Do You Like… Pattern
sections.body: Use DO (for I/you/we/they) and DOES (for he/she/it) to ask about preferences:

examples.en: Do you like music? — Yes, I do! / No, I don't.
examples.id: Apakah kamu suka musik? — Ya! / Tidak.

examples.en: Do you like football? — Yes, I do!
examples.id: Apakah kamu suka sepak bola? — Ya!

examples.en: Does she like cooking? — Yes, she does.
Does he like sports? — No, he doesn't.

sections.tip: Short answers: Yes, I do. / No, I don't. (NOT "Yes, I like" or "No, I not like")

sections.heading: Preference Conversation
sections.body: How to talk about likes naturally:

examples.en: B: No, I don't. But I like music!
examples.id: B: Tidak. Tapi saya suka musik!

examples.en: A: Does your friend like sports?
B: Yes, she does! She loves football.
examples.id: B: Ya! Dia sangat suka sepak bola.

content.sentence: — Do you like reading? — No, I ___.
content.explanation: Negative of "do" = don't (do not). "No, I don't." is the correct short answer.

content.hint: Say: Do you like football?

c5s5.title: Short Conversations
c5s5.intro: Now we put everything together into real short conversations. A conversation has flow — greeting, question, answer, follow-up. Let's practise the complete pattern.

sections.heading: Meeting a Friend
sections.body: A typical short conversation between two people who know each other:

examples.en: B: I am fine, thank you! And you?
examples.id: B: Saya baik, terima kasih! Dan kamu?
A: Saya sangat baik, terima kasih!

sections.tip: Always return the question! When someone asks "How are you?", ask "And you?" back.

sections.heading: Conversation Starters & Closers
sections.body: Phrases to open and close any English conversation:

examples.en: Question: How are you? / What's up?
See you + time: See you tomorrow! / See you later!

content.question: Bagaimana mengatakan 'Aku baik-baik saja' dalam bahasa Inggris?
content.explanation: "I am fine." = Saya baik-baik saja. It is the most common response to "How are you?"

content.phrase: How are you? I am fine, thank you!
content.hint: Say: How are you? I am fine, thank you!
content.translation: Apa kabar? Saya baik-baik saja, terima kasih!

c5s6.title: Final Challenge — Full Conversations
c5s6.intro: This is the final stage! Bring together everything from all 5 chapters: greetings, polite words, introductions, vocabulary, grammar, and full conversations.

sections.heading: The Complete English Conversation
sections.body: Here is a model conversation using everything you have learned:

examples.en: A: Good morning! My name is Rina. Nice to meet you!
examples.id: A: Selamat pagi! Nama saya Rina. Senang bertemu denganmu!

examples.en: B: Good morning Rina! I am from Bali. Where are you from?
examples.id: B: Selamat pagi Rina! Saya dari Bali. Kamu dari mana?

examples.en: A: I am from Jakarta. I am thirteen years old. Are you a student?
examples.id: A: Saya dari Jakarta. Saya 13 tahun. Apakah kamu pelajar?

examples.en: B: Yes, I am! Do you like sports?
examples.id: B: Ya! Apakah kamu suka olahraga?

examples.en: A: Yes, I do! I like football. Goodbye, and nice to meet you!
examples.id: A: Ya! Saya suka sepak bola. Selamat tinggal dan senang bertemu denganmu!
B: Selamat tinggal! Sampai jumpa besok!

sections.heading: Everything You Have Learned
sections.body: Congratulations! Here is a summary of all key patterns from all 5 chapters:

examples.en: Ch.1: Hello / Thank you / My name is / I am
Ch.2: This is a red book / I have two cats
Ch.3: I go to school / What do you eat?
Ch.4: She is tall and young / They are kind
Ch.5: Where are you from? / Do you like music?

sections.tip: Practice every day! Even one sentence a day will make a huge difference over time.

content.question: Terjemahkan percakapan singkat: 'Halo! Apa kabar? — Baik, terima kasih!'
options: Hello! How are you? — Fine, thank you!
Hello! What is your name? — I am fine!
Good morning! Where are you from? — I am good!
content.correctAnswer: Hello! How are you? — Fine, thank you!
content.explanation: Halo = Hello, Apa kabar = How are you, Baik = Fine/Good, Terima kasih = thank you.

content.phrase: Good morning! My name is Rina. Nice to meet you!
content.hint: Say a full greeting + introduction. You can use your real name.
content.translation: Selamat pagi! Nama saya Rina. Senang bertemu denganmu!
